paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. God doesn't send His people out because the crowd is ready. He tells Ezekiel the house of Israel is rebellious and won't listen, and He sends him anyway (Ezekiel 3:7). The job was never to get a good review. The job was to speak, "whether they listen or refuse to listen" (Ezekiel 2:5).

Now look at how God gets him ready, because that's the part I love. First the Spirit sets Ezekiel on his feet (Ezekiel 2:2). Then God tells him to eat the scroll, and it tastes "as sweet as honey" (Ezekiel 3:3). Friend, I think that means you take God's words in FIRST, all the way down, before you hand them to anybody. And God doesn't send him empty-handed either. He promises to make Ezekiel's forehead "like a diamond, harder than flint" (Ezekiel 3:9), so what He asks, He supplies.

So why does it matter to you, baker? Some days God's Word will taste sweet and your walk will still feel heavy, and Ezekiel went off in bitterness and sat overwhelmed for seven days (Ezekiel 3:14-15). I think that tells us it's okay to feel the weight, as long as you keep eating what God gives you. His strong hand was upon Ezekiel the whole way, and that same God is the One who gives you His Word (Ezekiel 3:14). Chew on that, friend.
